sanskrit: samudrād ūrmir madhumām̐ ud ārad upāṃśunā sam amṛtatvam ānaṭ | ghṛtasya nāma guhyaṃ yad asti jihvā devānām amṛtasya nābhiḥ ||
english: From the ocean a honey-sweet wave has risen up; in silence it has reached to immortality. The secret name of ghee that exists — it is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.

sanskrit: vayaṃ nāma pra bravāmā ghṛtasya- -asmin yajñe dhārayāmā namobhiḥ | upa brahmā śṛṇavac chasyamānaṃ catuḥśṛṅgo 'vamīd gaura etat ||
english: We shall proclaim the name of ghee; at this sacrifice we sustain it with reverences. Let the brahman hear it as it is chanted: the four-horned wild bull lowed it forth.

sanskrit: catvāri śṛṅgā trayo asya pādā dve śīrṣe sapta hastāso asya | tridhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti maho devo martyām̐ ā viveśa ||
english: Four are his horns, three are his feet, two are his heads, seven are his hands. Thrice-bound, the bull bellows aloud; the great god has entered into mortals.

sanskrit: tridhā hitaṃ paṇibhir guhyamānaṃ gavi devāso ghṛtam anv avindan | indra ekaṃ sūrya ekaṃ jajāna venād ekaṃ svadhayā niṣ ṭatakṣuḥ ||
english: Placed in three parts, hidden away by the Paṇis, the gods found the ghee within the cow. One part Indra engendered, one part Sūrya; one part they fashioned out by inspiration through the power of Svadhā.

sanskrit: etā arṣanti hṛdyāt samudrāc chatavrajā ripuṇā nāvacakṣe | ghṛtasya dhārā abhi cākaśīmi hiraṇyayo vetaso madhya āsām ||
english: These flow forth from the heart, from the inner ocean, possessed of a hundred enclosures — the enemy does not perceive them. I behold the streams of ghee; golden is the reed-grass in their midst.

sanskrit: samyak sravanti sarito na dhenā antar hṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ | ete arṣanty ūrmayo ghṛtasya mṛgā iva kṣipaṇor īṣamāṇāḥ ||
english: They flow together aright like rivers, like milk-cows, purified inwardly by heart and mind. These waves of ghee rush forth like deer driven forward by the bowstring.

sanskrit: sindhor iva prādhvane śūghanāso vātaḥ pramīyaḥ patayanti yahvāḥ | ghṛtasya dhārā aruṣo na vājī kāṣṭhā bhindann ūrmibhiḥ pinvamānaḥ ||
english: Like the roar that precedes the Sindhu, their rushing voices — the great ones fly like a wind that sweeps away. The stream of ghee, like a red prize-horse splitting the courses, swells with its waves.

sanskrit: abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣāḥ kalyāṇyaḥ smayamānāso agnim | ghṛtasya dhārāḥ samidho nasanta tā juṣāṇo haryati jātavedāḥ ||
english: Like fair women going to a tryst, radiant and smiling, they flow toward Agni. The streams of ghee rush to the kindling-sticks; delighting in them, Jātavedas rejoices.

sanskrit: kanyā iva vahatum etavā u añjy añjānā abhi cākaśīmi | yatra somaḥ sūyate yatra yajño ghṛtasya dhārā abhi tat pavante ||
english: I behold them, adorning themselves like maidens going to a wedding, anointing themselves. Where Soma is pressed, where the sacrifice is performed — toward that the streams of ghee flow clear.

sanskrit: abhy arṣata suṣṭutiṃ gavyam ājīm asmāsu bhadrā draviṇāni dhatta | imaṃ yajñaṃ nayata devatā no ghṛtasya dhārā madhumat pavante ||
english: Rush forward to the praise, to the contest for cattle; place auspicious treasures in us. Lead this sacrifice, O deities — the streams of ghee flow forth sweet as honey.

sanskrit: dhāman te viśvaṃ bhuvanam adhi śritam antaḥ samudre hṛdy antar āyuṣi | apām anīkāt samithād ya ābhṛtas tam aśyāma madhumantaṃ ta ūrmim ||
english: Upon your abode all existence is established — in the inner ocean, within the heart, within life. That wave of yours, sweet as honey, which has been brought from the face of the waters, from the confluence — may we attain it.

sanskrit: dve virūpe carataḥ svarthe anyānyā vatsam upa dhāpayete | harir anyasyāṃ bhavati svadhāvāñ chukro anyasyāṃ dadṛśe suvarcāḥ ||
english: Two of differing form wander, each seeking its own goal; each in turn suckles the calf. In one he appears tawny, self-sustaining; in the other he is seen white, of brilliant radiance.

sanskrit: daśemaṃ tvaṣṭur janayanta garbham atandrāso yuvatayo vibhṛtram | tigmānīkaṃ svayaśasaṃ janeṣu virocamānaṃ pari ṣīṃ nayanti ||
english: Ten young women, unwearied, who carry the embryo of Tvaṣṭr, lead it round — it of sharp edge, self-resplendent among peoples, shining brightly.

sanskrit: trīṇī jānāt prati bhūṣanty asya samudra ekaṃ divy ekam apsu | pūrvām anu pra diśaṃ pārthivānām ṛtūn praśāsad vi dadhāv anuṣṭhu ||
english: They adorn three of his births — one in the ocean, one in the sky, one in the waters. Following the eastward direction of earthly beings, he ruled the seasons and distributed them in due order.

sanskrit: ka imaṃ vo niṇyam ā ciketa vatso mātṝr janayata svadhābhiḥ | bahvīnāṃ garbho apasām upasthān mahān kavir niś carati svadhāvān ||
english: Who among you has comprehended this secret? The calf has begotten the mothers through inherent powers. The embryo of the many active waters, resting in their lap — the great seer moves forth, self-sustaining.

sanskrit: āviṣṭyo vardhate cārur āsu jihmānām ūrdhvaḥ svayasām upasthe | ubhe tvaṣṭur bibhyatur jāyamānāt pratīcī siṃhaṃ prati joṣayete ||
english: Possessing them, the beautiful one grows — upright in the lap of the crooked ones, in the self-sustained. Both, fearing the one being born of Tvaṣṭr, facing westward, welcome the lion.

sanskrit: ubhe bhadre joṣayete na mene gāvo na vāśrā upa tasthur evaiḥ | sa dakṣāṇāṃ dakṣapatir babhūva- -añjanti yaṃ dakṣiṇato havirbhiḥ ||
english: Both auspicious ones take pleasure in him, not proudly; neither the cows nor the calves stood near them with their tracks. He became the lord of the wise among the wise; they anoint him from the south with oblations.

sanskrit: ud yaṃyamīti saviteva bāhū ubhe sicau yatate bhīma ṛñjan | uc chukram atkam ajate simasmān navā mātṛbhyo vasanā jahāti ||
english: He stretches both arms upward like Savitṛ, the terrible one straining at both flanks. He shoots up a bright garment from himself; he sheds the new garments from the mothers.

sanskrit: tveṣaṃ rūpaṃ kṛṇuta uttaraṃ yat saṃpṛñcānaḥ sadanaṃ gobhir adbhiḥ | kavir budhnaṃ pari marmṛjyate dhīḥ sā devatātā samitir babhūva ||
english: He makes a brilliant, supreme form when he mingles his dwelling with rays of light and waters. The seer-vision cleanses the foundation thoroughly; that has become the gathering of the divine host.

sanskrit: uru te jrayaḥ pary eti budhnaṃ virocamānaṃ mahiṣasya dhāma | viśvebhir agne svayaśobhir iddho 'dabdhebhiḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhy asmān ||
english: Broadly your course goes around the foundation, the brightly shining abode of the great bull. O Agni, kindled by all self-resplendent ones, guard us with your undeceivable guardians.

sanskrit: dhanvaṃ srotaḥ kṛṇute gātum ūrmiṃ śukrair ūrmibhir abhi nakṣati kṣām | viśvā sanāni jaṭhareṣu dhatte 'ntar navāsu carati prasūṣu ||
english: He makes the desert a stream, a path, a wave; with bright waves he reaches the earth. He bears all prizes within his womb; he moves within the newly delivered mothers.

sanskrit: evā no agne samidhā vṛdhāno revat pāvaka śravasā vi bhāhi | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ||
english: Thus, O Agni, growing through the kindling-sticks, shine brilliantly upon us, O purifier, with splendor. May Mitra and Varuṇa magnify that for us, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven.

sanskrit: yo jāmadagnya iha kauśiko ya ātreya uta kāśyapo yaḥ | bharadvājā gotamā ye vasiṣṭhās tebhyaḥ pra brūma iha kilbiṣāṇi ||
english: He who is of the lineage of Jamadagni here, he who is a Kauśika, he who is of the lineage of Atri, and he who is a Kāśyapa — the Bharadvājas, Gotamas, and those who are Vasiṣṭhas — to them we here declare the transgressions.

sanskrit: agastyayaḥ kaṇvāḥ kutsāḥ prasravaṇā virūpā gargā mudgalā yaskāḥ śūnakāḥ | saṃkṛtayo brāhmaṇā ye na drugdhās tebhyaḥ pra brūma iha kilbiṣāṇi ||
english: The Agastyas, Kaṇvas, Kutsas, Prasravaṇas, Virūpas, Gargas, Mudgalas, Yaskas, Śūnakas — the Saṃkṛtis, all brāhmaṇas who have not been wronged — to them we here declare the transgressions.

sanskrit: yo nottiṣṭhād brāhmaṇe nādhamāne māndyena dṛpta uta dhairyeṇa | viśve devā upadraṣṭāro 'sya tasmin viṣaṃ saṃ nayān kilbiṣyam ||
english: He who does not rise to help a brāhmaṇa in distress, whether through sloth, pride, or stubbornness — all the Viśve Devās are witnesses against him; may the guilt, the poison, converge upon him.

sanskrit: yā ropayaḥ kilbiṣe brāhmaṇasya yāni caināṃsi bahudhā duṣkṛtāni | anutiṣṭhan prokta ātmani taṃ ni dhatte tathā tad devā uta veśayanti ||
english: Whatever festering wounds of guilt belong to a brāhmaṇa, whatever evil deeds done in many ways — he who follows along when instructed places them within himself; thus the gods also cause them to lodge in him.

sanskrit: nāśnīyān na piben na śayīta na niṃsīta jāyāṃ nota putram | brahmakilbiṣe prokta ud eva tiṣṭhet sa ṛtasya panthāḥ ||
english: He shall not eat, shall not drink, shall not lie down, shall not kiss wife nor son — one instructed in brahman-guilt should simply rise up and stand; that is the path of cosmic order.

sanskrit: śatarcino mādhyamā ye maharṣayaḥ kṣudrasūktānām uta yā prajeha | ṛṣīṇāṃ yāni janimāni vidmas tebhyaḥ pra brūma iha kilbiṣāṇi ||
english: The middling great seers of the hundred-versed hymns, and whatever progeny of the lesser hymns is here — the births of the seers that we know — to them we here declare the transgressions.

sanskrit: sodaryāṇāṃ pañcadaśānāṃ śatānāṃ trayastriṃśad ud aśiṣyanta devāḥ | ekasmin viddhe sarve 'rupyaṃ tad brāhmaṇe kilbiṣam anv avindan ||
english: Of the fifteen hundreds of brothers, thirty-three gods arose as pupils. When one was pierced, all were wounded; they found that guilt resting upon the brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tasmai sa druhyād ya idaṃ nāyad yo nottiṣṭhād yo na vadātā asmin | brāhmaṇasya kilbiṣe nāthitasya sodaryatām icchato brāhmaṇeṣu ||
english: He who did not bring this, he who did not rise, he who did not speak up in this matter — he acts treacherously against that brāhmaṇa; he who, though the brāhmaṇa was in distress, sought brotherhood among brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhad brāhmaṇāḥ saṃ vadadhvaṃ jītaṃ yācāma punar aitu sarvam | indrāgnī viśve devās te me jītaṃ punar ā vartayantu ||
english: Rise up, O brāhmaṇas, speak together; let us demand back what was won — may it all return. May Indra and Agni, may all the Viśve Devās turn what was won back to me again.

sanskrit: sa dīrgham āyuṣ kṛṇute sa prajāyai cikitsati | yo brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇo hūto anveti kilbiṣe ||
english: He secures long life; he attends to progeny — the brāhmaṇa who, himself a brāhmaṇa, when called follows in the matter of guilt.

sanskrit: nāsya prajāṃ śarvo hanti na rudro hanti nāśaniḥ | yo brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇaḥ satye vadati kilbiṣe ||
english: Neither Śarva smites his progeny, nor Rudra smites it, nor the thunderbolt — he, the brāhmaṇa, who truthfully speaks in the matter of a brāhmaṇa's guilt.

sanskrit: taṃ somapītho juṣate nṛcakṣā grāvabhiḥ saha | yo brāhmaṇasyāstāṃ hṛdaḥ sūrya ivāpālupat tamaḥ ||
english: The drinking of Soma delights him, the one who sees into men, together with the pressing-stones — he who stripped away the darkness from the standing heart of a brāhmaṇa as the sun strips away darkness.

sanskrit: ya utthāya kilbiṣe brāhmaṇasyānnasīcchann avāyati | ubhe enaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī saṃ tapatām athaitv agatasya panthām ||
english: He who, rising up in the matter of a brāhmaṇa's guilt, departs seeking food — let both Heaven and Earth scorch him; then let him go the path of one who has not gone.
